---
title: "estiMINT: EIR and HBR"
---

estiMINT supplies the EIR the emulator runs from. It inverts a prevalence or an HBR into the
EIR that would sustain it, and converts between EIR and HBR in both directions.

Everything it returns is an equilibrium value at the campaign. The trajectories come from
[stateMINT](../05-statemint/index.qmd).

::: {.chapter-outline}
- [Nets and dn0](nets-and-dn0.qmd) — `calculate_dn0`, `net_types`, and resistance.
- [Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd) — the `prevalence` model.
- [EIR and HBR](eir-and-hbr.qmd) — the `hbr` and `eir_to_hbr` models, and the error in converting back.
- [Mosquito density and EIR](mosquito-density.qmd) — `estimate_eir_with_mosquito_delta`.
- [estiMINT API](api.qmd) — every function and dataclass.
:::

## The three models

estiMINT ships three gradient-boosted models inside the wheel, each mapping one driving input
to one output while holding the same six covariates fixed. Nothing is downloaded. Pick the model
whose driving input you measured.

| Model name | Driving input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `"prevalence"` | `prev_y9` (parasite prevalence) | EIR |
| `"eir_to_hbr"` | `eir` | HBR |
| `"hbr"` | `hbr_y9` (human biting rate) | EIR |

Each model is named for its *input*, so the model named `"hbr"` takes an HBR and returns an EIR.

All three are loaded by name with `load_xgb_model` and called with `run_xgb_model`, and the six
shared covariates (`dn0_use`, `Q0`, `phi_bednets`, `seasonal`, `itn_use` and `irs_use`) describe
the setting, though two of them are not survey quantities at all and come out of `calculate_dn0`
instead. Most errors made with the package start there. Please see
[Nets and dn0](nets-and-dn0.qmd) for that calculation.
